page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7t.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The instance allocates 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. System memory totals 32.0 GB, providing an allocation ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware instruction extensions include AVX-512 foundational and VNNI extensions, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration.

Hardware resource provisioning excludes dedicated local storage and graphical processing units, requiring external network-attached block storage for persistence. Network connectivity is supported with a baseline throughput of 10 Gbps. Synthetic memory tests indicate large-block uncached read speeds of 95.55 GB/s and write speeds of 56.68 GB/s, while cached read bandwidth reaches 846.98 GB/s.

Benchmark evaluations position the ecs.c7t.4xlarge within the median range across standard x86 compute workloads. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 21,125.85 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,553.0. In application-specific testing, it processes 15.82 million Redis SET operations per second and handles static web serving at 21.07 GB/s. Small model LLM inference reaches 1,299.46 prompt processing tokens per second, though larger 70-billion-parameter models cannot run due to memory constraints.

Given its compute-heavy 1:2 memory-to-vCPU distribution and lack of local storage, the instance delivers predictable multi-threaded CPU execution. It is suited for CPU-bound tasks such as web serving fleets, software compilation, batch processing, and microservice backends that do not require massive resident memory pools.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7t.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture using an Intel Xeon 8369B processor clocked at 2.7 GHz. It provides 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores, coupled with 32.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio. The configuration includes AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware acceleration, a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps, and zero local disk storage, necessitating remote block storage. In standardized benchmarks, the instance yields average mid-tier throughput, recording a PassMark CPU score of 21,125.85, a multi-core Geekbench rating of 9,553.0, and Redis throughput of 15.82 million SET operations per second. Lacking an integrated GPU or dense memory footprint, the ecs.c7t.4xlarge is designed for distributed microservices, static web traffic handling, software build systems, and continuous integration pipelines prioritizing dedicated CPU resources over memory density.
